nodes.label: alert() Function
nodes.description: Pine Script function for creating dynamic alert events in indicators and strategies; supports dynamic messages, works in both script types, programmer controls frequency

nodes.label: alertcondition() Function
nodes.description: Pine Script function for creating individual alertcondition events in indicators only; accepts const string messages with optional placeholders

nodes.label: Order Fill Alert Events
nodes.description: Strategy-specific alert events triggered when broker emulator fills orders; customizable via alert_message parameter in strategy order functions

nodes.label: alert_message Parameter
nodes.description: Series string parameter in strategy order functions (strategy.close, strategy.entry, strategy.exit, strategy.order) for custom order fill alert messages

nodes.label: Alert Placeholders
nodes.description: Dynamic placeholders for alertcondition() messages: {{exchange}}, {{interval}}, {{open}}, {{high}}, {{low}}, {{close}}, {{volume}}, {{plot_N}}, {{plot(title)}}, {{ticker}}, {{time}}, {{timenow}}

nodes.label: Avoiding Repainting in Alerts
nodes.description: Technique to prevent alert repainting by configuring alerts to trigger only on close of realtime bar using Once Per Bar Close frequency

nodes.label: barstate.isfirst
nodes.description: Built-in variable true only on the dataset's first bar (bar_index == 0); useful for initializing variables once

nodes.label: barstate.islast
nodes.description: Built-in variable true if current bar is the last one on the chart; useful for restricting code execution to last bar for drawings

nodes.label: barstate.ishistory
nodes.description: Built-in variable true on all historical bars; mutually exclusive with barstate.isrealtime

nodes.label: barstate.isrealtime
nodes.description: Built-in variable true if current data update is a real-time bar update; barstate.islast is also true on all realtime bars

nodes.label: barstate.isnew
nodes.description: Built-in variable true on all historical bars and on the realtime bar's first (opening) update; useful for resetting varip variables

nodes.label: barstate.isconfirmed
nodes.description: Built-in variable true on all historical bars and on last (closing) update of realtime bar; useful for avoiding repainting

nodes.label: barstate.islastconfirmedhistory
nodes.description: Built-in variable true if script executes on dataset's last bar when market is closed, or bar immediately preceding realtime bar if market is open

nodes.label: OHLCV Built-in Variables
nodes.description: Built-in variables open, high, low, close, volume; on historical bars hold fixed OHLCV values; on realtime bars vary between iterations except open

nodes.label: syminfo.* Built-in Variables
nodes.description: Namespace providing symbol information: basecurrency, currency, description, main_tickerid, mincontract, mintick, pointvalue, prefix, root, session, ticker, tickerid, timezone, type

nodes.label: timeframe.* Chart Timeframe Built-ins
nodes.description: Built-ins for chart timeframe info: timeframe.isseconds, isminutes, isintraday, isdaily, isweekly, ismonthly, isdwm, multiplier, period, main_period

nodes.label: Pine Script Input Functions
nodes.description: Family of input.*() functions for user-configurable script parameters: input(), input.int(), input.float(), input.bool(), input.color(), input.string(), input.text_area(), input.timeframe(), input.symbol(), input.source(), input.session(), input.time(), input.price(), input.enum()

nodes.label: Input Function Common Parameters
nodes.description: Parameters common to all input functions: defval, title, tooltip, inline, group, display, active; some also have options, minval, maxval, step, confirm

nodes.label: input.enum() Function
nodes.description: Input function creating a dropdown based on members of a declared enum type; provides strict control over allowed values

nodes.label: library() Declaration Statement
nodes.description: Special script declaration for Pine Script libraries; must be published before use; always open-source; can export functions, methods, UDTs, and enums

nodes.label: export Keyword
nodes.description: Mandatory keyword for library functions, methods, UDTs, and enums to make them accessible when imported by other scripts

nodes.label: import Statement
nodes.description: Statement for using published libraries: import <username>/<libraryName>/<libraryVersion> [as <alias>]; version must be specified explicitly

nodes.label: Library Qualified Type Control
nodes.description: Mechanism where simple/series keywords prefix parameter types in exported library functions to control qualified type of arguments and return values

nodes.label: ticker.heikinashi() Function
nodes.description: Creates a special ticker identifier for requesting Heikin-Ashi data via request.security(); HA values are synthetic averages unsuited for backtesting

nodes.label: ticker.renko() Function
nodes.description: Creates ticker ID for requesting Renko chart data via request.security(); Renko bars plot only price movements ignoring time and volume

nodes.label: ticker.linebreak() Function
nodes.description: Creates ticker ID for requesting Line Break chart data via request.security()

nodes.label: ticker.kagi() Function
nodes.description: Creates ticker ID for requesting Kagi chart data via request.security(); Kagi charts use continuous line changing direction on price passing threshold

nodes.label: ticker.pointfigure() Function
nodes.description: Creates ticker ID for requesting Point and Figure chart data via request.security(); PnF ignores time, plots X columns for rising and O columns for falling prices

nodes.label: request.security() Function
nodes.description: Core function for requesting data from other symbols, timeframes, or custom contexts; accepts symbol, timeframe, expression, gaps, lookahead, ignore_invalid_symbol, currency, calc_bars_count parameters

nodes.label: request.security_lower_tf() Function
nodes.description: Retrieves intrabar data from a timeframe lower than the chart timeframe; returns an array of values for all LTF bars within each chart bar

nodes.label: request.financial() Function
nodes.description: Retrieves financial data from FactSet for specified symbol, financial metric ID, and reporting period

nodes.label: request.economic() Function
nodes.description: Retrieves economic and industry data for specified country code and field

nodes.label: request.currency_rate() Function
nodes.description: Requests a daily rate to convert a value expressed in one currency to another

nodes.label: Dynamic Requests (Pine Script v6)
nodes.description: Pine Script v6 feature enabling request.*() calls to use series arguments, execute in local scopes, and support nested requests; enabled by default

nodes.label: gaps Parameter for request.*() Functions
nodes.description: Parameter controlling how request.*() handles nonexistent values; barmerge.gaps_on returns na; barmerge.gaps_off (default) fills with last confirmed values

nodes.label: lookahead Parameter for request.security()
nodes.description: Parameter in request.security() determining if future HTF bar values can be seen on historical bars; barmerge.lookahead_on with [1] offset is recommended non-repainting pattern

nodes.label: Repainting Definition
nodes.description: Script behavior causing historical vs realtime calculations or plots to behave differently; categories: widespread/acceptable, potentially misleading, unacceptable, unavoidable

nodes.label: Fluid Data Values (Repainting Cause)
nodes.description: Historical data has fixed OHLC; realtime bars have fluid high/low/close values causing scripts using these to repaint; solutions use barstate.isconfirmed, [1] offset, or open price

nodes.label: Future Leak with request.security()
nodes.description: Dangerous repainting when request.security() uses lookahead_on without [1] offset, showing future prices on historical bars; not allowed in publications

nodes.label: Dataset Variations (Repainting Cause)
nodes.description: Repainting caused by changes in dataset starting points (plan-dependent bar limits) or revision of historical data by exchanges/brokers

nodes.label: Time-Based Session Strings
nodes.description: Custom session definition using HHmm-HHmm:days format; used in time() and time_close() functions to check if bars belong to a session

nodes.label: Named Sessions
nodes.description: Exchange-defined subsession names (e.g., regular, extended, us_regular); retrieved via syminfo.session; used in ticker.new() and ticker.modify()

nodes.label: Session State Variables
nodes.description: Built-in session variables: session.ismarket, session.ispremarket, session.ispostmarket, session.isfirstbar, session.islastbar, session.regular, session.extended

nodes.label: strategy() Declaration Statement
nodes.description: Declaration for Pine Script strategy scripts; gives access to strategy.* namespace for simulating orders and retrieving strategy information

nodes.label: Strategy Broker Emulator
nodes.description: TradingView component simulating trades using available chart data; fills orders after bar close on historical bars; makes assumptions about intrabar price movement

nodes.label: Bar Magnifier Backtesting Mode
nodes.description: Premium+ feature overriding broker emulator assumptions using lower-timeframe data for more precise order fills; enabled via use_bar_magnifier = true

nodes.label: Strategy Tester
nodes.description: TradingView tab visualizing hypothetical strategy performance with Overview, Performance Summary, List of Trades, and Properties sections

nodes.label: Pine Script Literal Strings
nodes.description: Character sequences up to 40,960 encoded characters enclosed by ASCII quotation marks or apostrophes; immutable values

nodes.label: String Escape Sequences
nodes.description: Backslash escape sequences in Pine strings: \n (newline), \t (horizontal tab), \\ (literal backslash), \' (literal apostrophe)

nodes.label: str.* String Functions Namespace
nodes.description: Specialized functions for constructing, inspecting, and modifying strings in Pine Script

nodes.label: UNIX Timestamps in Pine Script
nodes.description: Native time format in Pine; int value representing milliseconds since UNIX Epoch (Jan 1, 1970 UTC); time zone-agnostic; formatted with str.format_time()

nodes.label: Exchange Time Zone
nodes.description: Time zone of the instrument's exchange; calendar-based variables (month, dayofweek, hour) hold values in exchange TZ; accessible via syminfo.timezone

nodes.label: Timeframe String Specifications
nodes.description: Format for timeframe strings: multiplier + unit letter (T=ticks, S=seconds, D=days, W=weeks, M=months; no letter for minutes); e.g., 1S, 30, 1D, 3M

nodes.label: timeframe.in_seconds() Function
nodes.description: Converts a timeframe string to float seconds; useful for comparing timeframes using a universal unit

nodes.label: CE10101: Non-bool Condition Error
nodes.description: Compilation error when non-bool value used as condition in Pine v6; unlike v5, numerical values not implicitly cast to bool; fix with bool() or not na()

nodes.label: CW10003: Function Scope Consistency Warning
nodes.description: Compiler warning when functions depending on historical series are called conditionally rather than on every bar; fix by moving calls to global scope

nodes.label: RE10139: Memory Limits Exceeded Error
nodes.description: Runtime error from excessive memory consumption; common causes: returning collections from request.*() on every bar, excessive drawings, inefficient max_bars_back use

nodes.label: RE10143: Historical Buffer Limit Error
nodes.description: Runtime error when script tries to access historical values beyond the buffer limit; fix with max_bars_back() function or max_bars_back parameter

nodes.label: Alert Types Comparison FAQ
nodes.description: FAQ comparing alert() vs alertcondition() vs order fill events: usability, options for creating, activation mechanism, messages, and limitations

nodes.label: JSON Alert Messages FAQ
nodes.description: FAQ showing three methods to create JSON alert messages: static strings, placeholders, and dynamic string concatenation via str.* functions

nodes.label: Discord/Telegram Alert Integration FAQ
nodes.description: FAQ explaining how to send TradingView alerts to Discord via webhooks and to Telegram via intermediary service or custom server

nodes.label: Pine Script Data Structures FAQ
nodes.description: FAQ overview of Pine Script data structures: tuple (temporary grouping), array (ordered single-type), matrix (2D array), object (UDT instance), map (key-value pairs)

nodes.label: Variable Length Functions FAQ
nodes.description: FAQ on using variable lengths in built-in TA functions; some accept series lengths, others require simple int; ta library extends capabilities

nodes.label: Round to Increment FAQ
nodes.description: FAQ showing roundToIncrement() user-defined function pattern: math.round(value / increment) * increment

nodes.label: Real OHLC on Heikin Ashi Chart FAQ
nodes.description: FAQ explaining how to get real OHLC prices on non-standard charts using ticker.new() with syminfo.prefix/ticker and request.security()
nodes.norm_label: real ohlc on heikin ashi chart faq

nodes.label: Volume/Profile Indicator Limitation
nodes.description: Pine Script cannot replicate Volume Profile and similar indicators that require access to intrabar tick data. Approximations using PineCoders VisibleChart library exist.

nodes.label: TradingView Screener Integration Limitation
nodes.description: Pine Script indicators cannot directly interact with TradingView's screener. Scripts are limited to chart-based execution.

nodes.label: input.source() Function
nodes.description: input.source() allows scripts to receive a price series (e.g., close, open) as user input, enabling flexible source selection.

nodes.label: request.security() for HTF/LTF Data
nodes.description: request.security() fetches data from a different symbol or timeframe. For higher timeframe data, use barmerge.lookahead_on with close[1] offset to avoid repainting.

nodes.label: request.security_lower_tf() for Intrabar Analysis
nodes.description: request.security_lower_tf() fetches intrabar data at a lower timeframe, returning arrays of values per bar. Use barmerge.lookahead_off to avoid repainting on LTF data.

nodes.label: Repainting Avoidance with HTF Requests
nodes.description: To avoid repainting when using HTF data, use barmerge.lookahead_on combined with a [1] offset on the series (e.g., close[1]) to ensure only confirmed bar data is used.

nodes.label: timeframe.in_seconds() and timeframe.from_seconds()
nodes.description: timeframe.in_seconds() converts a timeframe string to seconds. timeframe.from_seconds() converts seconds back to a timeframe string.

nodes.label: Pine Script Scope (Global vs Local)
nodes.description: Pine Script distinguishes between global scope (top-level code) and local scope (inside functions, if/for/while blocks). Variables declared in local scope are not accessible from global scope.

nodes.label: Pine Logs for Debugging
nodes.description: Pine Script v5+ provides log.info(), log.warning(), log.error() functions to output debug messages to the Pine Logs panel.

nodes.label: User-Defined Types (UDTs) in Pine Script
nodes.description: UDTs are custom data structures (methodless classes) declared with the 'type' keyword. They allow grouping multiple fields of different types into one logical entity.

nodes.label: strategy() Declaration Function
nodes.description: strategy() declares a Pine Script strategy with parameters for name, overlay, initial capital, commission, slippage, and backtesting behavior.

nodes.label: strategy.entry() and strategy.exit()
nodes.description: strategy.entry() places entry orders; strategy.exit() places exit orders with stop-loss/take-profit parameters (stop, limit, profit, loss, trail_points, trail_offset).

nodes.label: Strategy Broker Emulator
nodes.description: The broker emulator simulates order execution during backtesting. Causes of repainting include calc_on_every_tick, calc_on_order_fills, and process_orders_on_close.

nodes.label: OCA Order Groups (strategy.oca.reduce)
nodes.description: strategy.oca.reduce creates one-cancels-all order groups where partial fills reduce the quantity of other orders in the group.

nodes.label: Strategy Backtesting Features
nodes.description: TradingView strategies support Bar Magnifier (intrabar order fills), Deep Backtesting (extended historical data), and Bar Replay for visual backtesting.

nodes.label: plotchar() and plotshape() for Static Text
nodes.description: plotchar() and plotshape() display text/characters on the chart but only accept 'const string' values — dynamic text requires label.new().
nodes.norm_label: plotchar() and plotshape() for static text

nodes.label: label.new() for Dynamic Text
nodes.description: label.new() creates labels with dynamic (series string) text. Supports full string expressions computed at runtime.

nodes.label: table.new() for Fixed-Position Text Display
nodes.description: table.new() creates fixed-position tables on the chart for displaying text in a grid layout. Tables do not scroll with the chart.

nodes.label: xloc.bar_index vs xloc.bar_time Limits
nodes.description: xloc.bar_index uses integer bar indices with a limited future range; xloc.bar_time uses UNIX timestamps allowing drawing further into the future.

nodes.label: Repainting Avoidance Without request.security()
nodes.description: To avoid repainting without using request.security(), use barstate.isconfirmed or [1] offset to only act on confirmed bar data.

nodes.label: On/Off Switch Pattern with var bool
nodes.description: A persistent boolean toggle using 'var bool switchState = false' toggled with ':= not switchState' implements an on/off switch across bars.
nodes.norm_label: on/off switch pattern with var bool

nodes.label: Pine Profiler for Performance Analysis
nodes.description: The Pine Profiler measures execution time and resource usage of Pine Script code to identify performance bottlenecks.

nodes.label: Chart Type Detection
nodes.description: chart.is_standard, chart.is_heikinashi, chart.is_renko, etc. detect the current chart type in Pine Script.

nodes.label: time Variable (UNIX Milliseconds)
nodes.description: The built-in 'time' variable holds the UNIX timestamp in milliseconds of the bar's opening time.

nodes.label: str.format_time() Function
nodes.description: str.format_time() formats a UNIX timestamp into a human-readable string with a specified format pattern and timezone.

nodes.label: Session Strings with time() Function
nodes.description: Session strings (e.g., '0930-1600') define trading session time ranges. The time() function tests whether the current bar falls within a specified session.

nodes.label: timeframe.change() Function
nodes.description: timeframe.change() returns true on the first bar of a new period in the specified timeframe, useful for detecting period boundaries.

nodes.label: close Variable for Current Price
nodes.description: The 'close' built-in variable returns the bar's closing price on confirmed bars and the current price on the realtime bar.

nodes.label: var Keyword for Persistent Variables
nodes.description: Variables declared with 'var' are initialized only once on the first bar and persist their values across all subsequent bars.

nodes.label: varip Keyword for Intrabar Persistence
nodes.description: Variables declared with 'varip' persist across intrabar ticks and are not rolled back on unconfirmed bars, unlike 'var' variables.

nodes.label: Assignment Operators (=, :=, ==)
nodes.description: = declares a new variable (initial assignment), := reassigns an existing variable, == tests equality. Confusing = and := is a common error.

nodes.label: na Value Behavior in Comparisons
nodes.description: na represents an undefined/missing value. Any arithmetic or comparison involving na produces na. Use na() to test and nz() to substitute defaults.

nodes.label: plot() Limitations
nodes.description: plot() calls cannot be placed inside if/for blocks. Conditional plotting is done by passing na instead of a value to hide the plot on certain bars.

nodes.label: Drawing Objects (line, label, box, polyline)
nodes.description: Pine Script drawing objects (line.new, label.new, box.new, polyline.new) create visual elements on the chart. Arrays of these objects (*.all) limit their total count.

nodes.label: Color Features (predefined, custom, gradient, fill)
nodes.description: Pine Script supports predefined colors (color.red etc.), custom hex colors, transparency via color.new(), gradient colors, and fill() between plots.

nodes.label: hline() Toggling
nodes.description: hline() creates horizontal lines at fixed price levels. To toggle visibility, use color.new(color, 100) for transparent and a visible color alternately.

nodes.label: Array Declaration in Pine Script
nodes.description: Arrays declared with array<type> or array.new<type>(). Support var/varip for persistence. array.from() creates arrays from literals.

nodes.label: Array Operations (push/pop/shift/unshift/insert/remove)
nodes.description: Arrays support stack operations (push/pop), queue operations (shift/unshift), and random access (insert/remove). Maximum 100,000 elements.

nodes.label: Array Calculations (avg/min/max/stdev)
nodes.description: Built-in array functions provide element-wise calculations: array.avg(), array.min(), array.max(), array.stdev(), array.sum(), array.mode().

nodes.label: Array Searching (includes/indexof/binary_search)
nodes.description: array.includes() checks membership, array.indexof() finds position, array.binary_search() performs binary search on sorted arrays.

nodes.label: Pine Script Built-in Namespaces
nodes.description: Pine Script organizes built-ins by namespace: ta.* (technical analysis), math.* (math functions), str.* (string operations), request.* (data requests), input.* (user inputs), color.* (colors), strategy.* (trading strategies).

nodes.label: Built-in Price and Volume Variables
nodes.description: Built-in variables: open, high, low, close, volume, hl2, hlc3, ohlc4 provide OHLCV data for each bar.

nodes.label: barstate.* Variables
nodes.description: barstate namespace provides: barstate.isfirst, barstate.islast, barstate.ishistory, barstate.isrealtime, barstate.isconfirmed, barstate.islastconfirmedhistory.

nodes.label: syminfo.* Variables
nodes.description: syminfo namespace provides symbol metadata: syminfo.ticker, syminfo.exchange, syminfo.currency, syminfo.mintick, syminfo.pointvalue, syminfo.timezone.

nodes.label: if/else if/else Conditional Structure
nodes.description: Pine Script if/else structures support both side-effect form (executing code) and value-returning form (returning last expression value). All branches must return compatible types.

nodes.label: switch Conditional Structure
nodes.description: switch structure matches an expression against cases (with expression) or evaluates conditions (without expression). Falls through to default case if no match. Can return values.

nodes.label: Enum Declaration with enum Keyword
nodes.description: Enums declared with 'enum EnumName\n    field1\n    field2' syntax. Fields can have optional string titles. Access members with dot notation (EnumName.field).

nodes.label: input.enum() for Enum Inputs
nodes.description: input.enum() creates a dropdown input with enum field titles. Field titles appear in the Settings/Inputs tab dropdown menu.

nodes.label: Enum Type Safety
nodes.description: Each enum is a unique type. Members of different enums cannot be compared or used interchangeably, even if they have identical names and titles.

nodes.label: Enum Shadowing Rules
nodes.description: Enum names cannot match built-in namespaces (e.g., ta, syminfo, polyline). This differs from UDTs which can shadow some built-in names.

nodes.label: Bar-by-Bar Execution Model
nodes.description: Pine Script executes scripts bar by bar from left to right on historical data, then continues on realtime bars. Each bar triggers one execution of the entire script.

nodes.label: Rollback on Realtime Bars
nodes.description: On realtime bars, Pine Script rolls back variable values to their last confirmed state before each new execution, except for varip variables.

nodes.label: Time Series Data Structure
nodes.description: Time series are Pine Script's core data structure. Each variable implicitly stores its historical values accessible via the [] history-referencing operator.

nodes.label: Historical Buffers (max 5000 bars)
nodes.description: Pine Script automatically manages historical buffers up to 5000 bars deep (auto-optimized). The max_bars_back parameter can extend buffers for specific series.

nodes.label: Identifier Naming Rules
nodes.description: Identifiers must start with a letter (A-Z, a-z) or underscore, followed by letters, underscores, or digits. Case-sensitive. Style Guide recommends SNAKE_CASE for constants, camelCase for others.

nodes.label: for Loop (Count-Controlled)
nodes.description: for loops iterate a counter from a start value to an end value with an optional step (by). Syntax: 'for counter = from to to_num [by step]'.

nodes.label: while Loop (Condition-Controlled)
nodes.description: while loops execute while a condition is true. Syntax: 'while condition'. Support break and continue keywords.

nodes.label: for...in Loop (Collection-Controlled)
nodes.description: for...in loops iterate over collections. Two forms: 'for item in collection' and 'for [index, item] in collection' for indexed access.

nodes.label: Map Declaration (map<keyType, valueType>)
nodes.description: Maps created with map.new<keyType, valueType>(). Support var/varip for persistence. Preserve insertion order for keys and values.

nodes.label: Map Operations (put/get/contains/remove/keys/values)
nodes.description: map.put() adds/updates key-value pairs, map.get() retrieves values, map.contains() checks key existence, map.remove() deletes pairs, map.keys()/map.values() return arrays.

nodes.label: Maps with Enum Keys
nodes.description: Maps can use enum types as keys (map<EnumType, valueType>), providing strict control over all allowed keys in the map.

nodes.label: Matrix Declaration (matrix<type>)
nodes.description: Matrices are 2D collections using matrix.new<type>(rows, cols, initial_value). Support var/varip for persistence. Maximum 100,000 elements.

nodes.label: Matrix Operations (get/set/fill/row/col/add_row/add_col)
nodes.description: matrix.get()/set() access elements by row/col indices. matrix.row()/col() return array copies. matrix.add_row()/add_col() insert rows/columns. matrix.remove_row()/remove_col() delete them.

nodes.label: Matrix Linear Algebra Operations
nodes.description: Pine Script matrices support: matrix.sum()/diff() (addition/subtraction), matrix.mult() (multiplication/dot product), matrix.det() (determinant), matrix.inv()/pinv() (inverse/pseudoinverse), matrix.transpose(), matrix.rank(), matrix.eigenvalues()/eigenvectors().

nodes.label: Matrix Inspection Functions
nodes.description: matrix.is_square(), matrix.is_identity(), matrix.is_diagonal(), matrix.is_symmetric(), matrix.is_antisymmetric(), matrix.is_triangular(), matrix.is_binary(), matrix.is_zero() inspect matrix properties.

nodes.label: Matrix Manipulation (reshape/reverse/transpose/sort/concat)
nodes.description: matrix.reshape() changes dimensions without changing element count. matrix.reverse() reverses element order. matrix.sort() sorts rows by column. matrix.concat() appends rows.

nodes.label: Built-in Methods for Special Types
nodes.description: Pine Script provides built-in methods for array, matrix, map, line, linefill, box, polyline, label, table, chart.point. Method syntax: object.method() instead of namespace.function(object).

nodes.label: User-Defined Methods
nodes.description: User-defined methods use 'method' keyword before function name. First parameter type must be explicitly declared and determines the type the method is associated with.

nodes.label: Method Overloading
nodes.description: Methods can be overloaded with the same name but different parameter types/signatures. The compiler selects the appropriate overload based on the type of the first parameter.

nodes.label: UDT Object Creation with .new()
nodes.description: Objects are UDT instances created with TypeName.new() or TypeName.new(field1Value, field2Value). Fields accessed with dot notation. Objects assigned by reference.

nodes.label: Shallow vs Deep Copy of Objects
nodes.description: TypeName.copy() creates a shallow copy where special type fields still reference same objects. Deep copies require explicitly copying nested fields.
nodes.norm_label: shallow vs deep copy of objects

nodes.label: UDT Shadowing Rules
nodes.description: UDT names can shadow built-in types like 'line' or 'table', but cannot use fundamental type names (int, float, string, bool, color) as UDT names.

nodes.label: Arithmetic Operators (+, -, *, /, %)
nodes.description: Pine Script arithmetic operators: +, -, *, /, %. Division of ints produces float. + also concatenates strings. % calculates modulo using floor division.

nodes.label: Comparison Operators (<, <=, !=, ==, >, >=)
nodes.description: Six comparison operators return bool. == and != work with any fundamental type including strings and colors. Other operators (<, <=, >, >=) only apply to numerical values.

nodes.label: ?: Ternary Operator
nodes.description: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. Can be chained for multi-branch logic. Does not create local scopes unlike if structures.

nodes.label: [] History-Referencing Operator
nodes.description: The [] operator accesses past values of time series. close[1] is previous bar's close. Returns na for indices beyond available history. Can only be used once per expression.

nodes.label: Operator Precedence Rules
nodes.description: Operator precedence order (highest to lowest): [] > unary +/-/not > *//%  > +/- > comparison > ==,!= > and > or > ?:. Use parentheses to override.

nodes.label: Compound Assignment Operators (+=, -=, *=, /=, %=)
nodes.description: Compound operators combine arithmetic with reassignment. x += 1 is equivalent to x := x + 1. += also concatenates strings.

nodes.label: Script Version Annotation (//@version=)
nodes.description: Scripts declare their Pine Script version with //@version=N (N from 1 to 6). Strongly recommended to use latest version. Placed at top of script.

nodes.label: Script Declaration Statement
nodes.description: All scripts must call one of: indicator(), strategy(), or library(). These set script type, name, and behavior properties.

nodes.label: Compiler Annotations
nodes.description: Compiler annotations: //@version=, //@description, //@function, //@param, //@returns, //@type, //@enum, //@field, //@variable, //@strategy_alert_message. Also //#region and //#endregion for collapsible code blocks.

nodes.label: Local Blocks and Scope
nodes.description: Local blocks use 4-space or tab indentation. Each defines a distinct local scope. Global scope statements cannot begin with whitespace.

nodes.label: Line Wrapping in Pine Script
nodes.description: Long lines can be wrapped across multiple lines. Wrapped lines cannot use multiples of 4 spaces indentation (to avoid ambiguity with local blocks), except inside parentheses.

nodes.label: Collection Type Templates
nodes.description: Collections (arrays, matrices, maps) use type templates like array<float>, matrix<int>, map<string, float> to specify contained types. Support built-in, UDT, and enum types.

nodes.label: Shallow Copy vs Deep Copy in Collections
nodes.description: Shallow copies share references to nested objects. Deep copies require explicit element-by-element copying. Affects arrays, matrices, maps, and UDT objects.
nodes.norm_label: shallow copy vs deep copy in collections

nodes.label: Type Qualifiers (const/input/simple/series)
nodes.description: Pine Script uses type qualifiers: const (compile-time), input (user input), simple (fixed after first bar), series (varies per bar). Expressions produce strongest qualifier from operands.
